children: By Jamie Chisholm
A rebound off lows for the S&P 500 on Wednesday calms bourses after AI wash out
Futures show the New York Stock Exchange may enjoy a positive session when traders return from Thanksgiving.

Wall Street is set for an upbeat return to action after European bourses tracked gains in Asian equities on Thursday, as global investors gave thanks to a stoic performance from their U.S. counterparts.

In electronic trading, the E-mini S&P 500 futures contract (ES00) was up 0.7%, pointing to a roughly 50-point gain for the index when traders return to their desks on Black Friday for a truncated session after the Thanksgiving break.

South Korea's Kospi index KR:180721 steadied after recent sharp falls, rising 0.3%. while Japan's Nikkei 225 JP:NIK added 0.9% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng HK:HSI climbed 1.2%. By afternoon in Europe, Germany's DAX index DX:DAX was up 1.9% and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 had climbed 1.5%.

"The rollercoaster [global] stock market is back on an upwards path as a new round of Trump tariffs aren't as bad as feared and the U.S. takes the day off to celebrate Thanksgiving," said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.

The rallies came after what had looked to be another dreadful session for U.S. stocks, with the S&P 500 initially falling 3.2% on Thanksgiving-Eve. However, Wall Street recovered its poise and its main equity barometer closed down just 0.25% as recently badly-battered AI-linked shares attracted a flurry of buyers.

Nvidia stock (NVDA), whose volatility following the sacking and return of CEO Jensen Huang has exemplified investor nervousness toward the AI trade, saw a 9.1% slide turn into a 1.3% gain. That's as shares in Anthropic (ANT), the AI tool maker that last week recorded the world's biggest ever IPO, saw a 12% rally off session lows.

Analysts welcomed the recovery as a sign that the market had found a level at which it has absorbed concerns about stubborn inflation and likely Federal Reserve rate hikes, looming additional tariffs, and fears that the AI buildout may be slowing.

The market has likely bottomed after its pullback from the highs of October, Tom Lee, head of research at Fundstrat said in video commentary posted late Wednesday. "The risk reward is really good, so instead of worrying about the next couple of weeks put on your investor hat."

Lee's Fundstrat colleague, head of technical strategy Mark Newton, said the market's ability to recoup most of Wednesday's early losses "is an encouraging development heading into the Thanksgiving holiday and speaks to buyers starting to show more interest on weakness."

But Newton also warned: "One intraday reversal does not change the fact that near-term trends remain negative across most major indices, and technology has yet to show the type of stabilization on weekly charts that normally accompanies a meaningful low."

Patrick Munnelly, market strategist at Tickmill Group, also welcomed the calmer tone across stock markets, but he added that "hot inflation data and fragile market structure continue to limit upside conviction."

"Thanksgiving brings surface-level stabilization, but neither the AI valuation debate nor the Federal Reserve's inflation fight has been resolved," he said. "For traders, immediate tactical focus centers on S&P 500 futures defending 7,200 in thin holiday volume."
Other analysts were more broadly upbeat as the stock market heads into what is traditionally a period of seasonal strength.

"We believe the recent market correction-particularly in the AI trade-is rooted in waning confidence and policy concerns rather than a fundamental flaw in the cycle," said Daniel Skelly, managing director, at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management.

"Because we continue to see solid economic and earnings dynamics, as well as accelerating demand for AI spending and adoption, we're recommending going on offense in AI-related ideas," Skelly said in a note to clients.
-Jamie Chisholm
